prs.title: [Bugfix][CI][Hardware][AMD] Fix various e4m3fn -> e4m3fnuz normalization issues
prs.author: mawong-amd
prs.body_head:
## Purpose
This PR fixes various issues in e4m3fnuz handling encountered by various quantization code paths (ModelOpt, online). In particular, on `e4m3fnuz` platforms, `normalize_e4m3fn_to_e4m3fnuz` should be called exactly once on a given FP8 linear layer after weights are loaded.
However,
- Some PyTorch linear kernel-based code paths used during ModelOpt quantization were not calling this function.
- Some code paths used in online quantization methods were trying to call this function twice, once in the linear layer and once more in the linear layer's kernel implementation.

The end result is that the Quantization test group should now be passing on ROCm.

This PR also removes a Quark mxfp4 model that was causing failures in the Kernels MoE test group because it is incompatible with HF Transformers v5.
## Test Plan
`VLLM_TEST_FORCE_LOAD_FORMAT=auto pytest -v -s quantization/ --ignore quantization/test_blackwell_moe.py`
`pytest -v -s kernels/moe --ignore=kernels/moe/test_modular_oai_triton_moe.py`
These tests should be run as part of the Quantization and Kernels MoE test groups in vLLM AMD CI.

## Test Result
The above test groups pass, and there are no regressions.

cc @kenroche and @AndreasKaratzas

prs.title: [ROCm][CI] Gate incompatible HF references on Transformers v5
prs.author: AndreasKaratzas
prs.body_head:
This updates generation-test metadata for models whose HF reference path is incompatible with the installed Transformers v5 runtime.

Test groups fixed:
- `mi355_1: Language Models Tests (Standard)` for MiniCPM4.
- `mi355_1: Language Models Test (Extended Generation)` for HyperCLOVAX.

MiniCPM4:
- Fails in HF remote code because it imports `is_torch_fx_available`, removed from the installed Transformers v5 runtime.
- Links the upstream compatibility request, which is closed as not planned: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/44561

HyperCLOVAX:
- The model's remote code imports `ROPE_INIT_FUNCTIONS` and unconditionally indexes `ROPE_INIT_FUNCTIONS[self.rope_type]`; for the default case, `self.rope_type` is `"default"`: https://huggingface.co/naver-hyperclovax/HyperCLOVAX-SEED-Think-14B/blob/main/modeling_hyperclovax.py
- Transformers v5 docs still list `"default"` as a valid RoPE type. The incompatibility is narrower: v5 no longer exposes a `"default"` entry in `ROPE_INIT_FUNCTIONS`, while v4.57 did. In v5's own Llama code, default RoPE is handled by `compute_default_rope_parameters`; `ROPE_INIT_FUNCTIONS` is consulted only when `rope_type != "default"`.
- The v5 migration guide also notes that rotary embedding configuration now lives under `config.rope_parameters`, which matches the new v5 model path.

cc @kenroche

prs.title: [ROCm][CI] Fix and stabilize EAGLE3 acceptance tests
prs.author: AndreasKaratzas
prs.body_head:
This updates the EAGLE3 acceptance length regression test to use ROCm backend auto-selection instead of hard-selecting attention backends. It adds ROCm-specific expected per-position acceptance values for gpt-oss without widening the default tolerance. The Qwen3-VL FP8 MoE case is limited to ROCm TP4 and enables expert parallelism to avoid the unsupported block-FP8 TP shard shape. The per-position check now treats lower-than-baseline acceptance as the regression signal, so improvements do not fail the test. 

cc @kenroche

prs.title: [AMD][CI][BugFix] Fix  Distributed Compile Unit Tests (2xH100-2xMI300) group
prs.author: rasmith
prs.body_head:
## Purpose
Multiple problems were encountered with the `Distributed Compile Unit Tests (2xH100-2xMI300)` tests.

For `test_tp2_ar_rms.py:`
* `disable_custom_all_reduce=False`  needed to be set for the fusion passes to initalize on ROCm. Leaving this disabled causes the tests to fail since the custom all-reduce setup will be skipped during initalization.
* On ROCm, `RocmAiterAllReduceFusionPass`  is used, so this test also needs to check patterns for `aiter_ar_rms_fusion` instead of `ar_rms_fusion`
    - added patterns to `FUSION_LOG_PATTERNS` in ` tests/compile/fusions_e2e/common.py`
    - update counts in `tests/compile/fusions_e2e/models.py` 
        + `llama3_8b`: `n_layers * 2` (dense MLP, all-reduce after both attn and MLP)
        + `qwen3_a3b`: `n_layers * 2`
        + `gpt_oss_20b`:` n_layers + 1` (MoE MLP has no all-reduce, only attn `o_proj`)
* Swap out the `ar_rms_fusion` pattern for `aiter_ar_rms_fusion` on ROCm in `test_tp2_ar_rms.py::test_tp2_ar_rms_fusion`
* Skip `openai/gpt-oss-20b` with `ROCM_ATTN` backend due to the following error:
` ValueError: Selected backend AttentionBackendEnum.ROCM_ATTN is not valid for this configuration. Reason: ['attention sinks not supported]`

For `test_async_tp.py`:
* ` async_tp_pass_on_test_model ` tries to use port 12345, but on some systems `alloy `will be running which will use the same port
     - find an open port and use that instead
 * `AsyncTPPass `does not check if CUTLASS is available before registering the `CutlassScaledMMReduceScatterPattern` and `AllGatherCutlassScaledMMPattern `patterns

      - wrap these parameters using `param `and `skipif` `cutlass_scaled_mm` is not available.

prs.title: [ROCm][CI] Fix ROCm LoRA Transformers fallback with full CUDA graphs
prs.author: AndreasKaratzas
prs.body_head:
Fixes `LoRA %N`

- Restrict the gfx950 `wvSplitKrc` skinny GEMM path to 2D activations.
- Make the vLLM C RMSNorm provider flatten N-D activations by token row and reshape back.
- Initialize torch-compile support on the actual HF decoder instance for dynamic remote-code classes.

The original failure was `Unsupported N value: 512,2048,1` in `wvSplitKrc`. The selector counted flattened tokens from a 3D Transformers activation, but `wvSplitKrc` reads `size(0)` and is only correct for 2D row-major inputs. After fixing that selector bug, full decode graph capture exposed the same N-D activation mismatch in the `vllm_c` RMSNorm provider. Flattening RMSNorm inputs matches its row-wise kernel contract and preserves the public tensor shape.

- Known-good commit: `0e39202ca911319c7747a2f9d5a0c162fdff4fd9`.
- Failing commit observed in CI: `7845379230c48c9103ab71682ee05977dfbbdfce`.
- The likely trigger is the update to transformers v5

cc @kenroche

prs.title: [CI] set max transformers version for skywork model
prs.author: divakar-amd
prs.body_head:
This PR resolves the following error:
```
AttributeError: 'SkyworkChatModel' object has no attribute 'all_tied_weights_keys'.
Did you mean: '_tied_weights_keys'?
```
The failure occurs because of change in `transformers 5.x` APIs which introduced `all_tied_weights_keys`

In transformers 5.x post_init() now sets an instance attribute all_tied_weights_keys (a dict):

This PR resolves the following tests as shown in this [AMD CI run](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/8323/summary?sid=019e062c-1021-4484-918f-af6e7efe7df4&tab=output)

prs.title: [ROCm][CI] Accept Different But Valid Output for `test_olmoe_tp`
prs.author: micah-wil
prs.body_head:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
We're seeing some failures in `LoRA TP Test (Distributed)` on AMD MI355 CI pipeline https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/5300/steps/canvas?sid=019c8e72-d91a-42ee-8022-a42c57625216&tab=output#019c8e72-da1d-4fc3-95e4-3f73d89abcad/L1235. There are two issues. The first is that sometimes the output includes comments at the end explaining the SQL query output, but once I conditioned the prompt template to tell it to not do that, this issue was resolved. The second issue is that it outputs a different output than the expected one, but it is still valid. I've just included it as a valid response in the test.
